channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan to increase Russian gas imports amid potential US sanctions
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to boost natural gas imports from Russia under a new agreement with Gazprom. The deal involves purchasing approximately 11 billion cubic meters of gas this year, with further talks for 2027. This move comes as Kazakhstan faces surging domestic demand despite being a net exporter, and as Russia faces potential US sanctions on its energy sector.

item.title: Russia instigates trade disputes within Eurasian Economic Union
item.description: Russia is reportedly initiating trade conflicts with fellow Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) members, including Kazakhstan and Armenia, while engaged in military actions in Ukraine. These actions contradict the EAEU's aim of promoting free trade. Moscow has imposed trade bans on Armenian goods and cut off gas supplies, citing Armenia's closer ties with the European Union.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Orders Investigation into Soldier Deaths
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev chaired a commission meeting following the deaths of servicemen during military exercises in the Mangystau region. A criminal case has been initiated, and an interdepartmental investigative team is working to establish the circumstances and identify those responsible. Families of the deceased will receive state support.

item.title: US and Uzbekistan to cooperate on nuclear energy safety and operations
item.description: The United States and Uzbekistan signed a memorandum of understanding to cooperate on nuclear energy operations and safety issues. The agreement covers monitoring, safe operations, disaster response, and improving regulatory guidelines and training programs.

item.title: Uzbekistan plans Caspian and Black Sea logistics hubs for Middle Corridor trade
item.description: Uzbekistan intends to establish logistics facilities on the Caspian and Black Seas to support its Middle Corridor trade agenda. Agreements are in place for facilities in Georgia's Poti port, with plans to develop infrastructure in Aktau, Turkmenbashi, and Baku.

item.title: Kremlin sends congratulatory note to Armenia's Pashinyan on Independence Day
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin sent a congratulatory note to Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan on Armenia's 35th anniversary of re-independence. The message, also echoed by other Russian officials, emphasized maintaining comprehensive Russian-Armenian cooperation.

item.title: Uzbek Company Mega Plast Group Focuses on High-Quality Polyethylene Pipes for Infrastructure
item.description: Uzbekistan's Mega Plast Group produces high-pressure polyethylene pipes and drip irrigation systems for water supply, energy, and agriculture. The company, operating since 2016, emphasizes product quality and increased production volume. They have secured credit funds and purchased new equipment to meet growing demand.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Meets BlackRock Leadership in New York to Discuss Tashkent Financial Center
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration, met with BlackRock executives in New York to discuss establishing the Tashkent International Financial Center by 2027. Discussions also covered Uzbekistan's development prospects, with Mirziyoyeva noting the country is becoming a hub for significant investments.

item.title: Russian President Putin Expresses Condolences to Kazakhstan Over Sailor Deaths in Caspian Sea
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin sent condolences to Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev following a tragic incident during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. Seventeen Kazakh sailors were swept out to sea in bad weather; twelve died, three were rescued, and two remain missing. Criminal cases have been opened.

item.title: Uzbekistan prioritizes education as key to national development and human capital
item.description: Uzbekistan's government views education and youth intellectual development as a crucial long-term investment. President outlined seven national programs to boost the country's development, focusing on strengthening economic and social potential. Knowledge and skills are identified as the primary capital for future growth, with a focus on quality education and teacher development.

item.title: Tashkent hosts 'Future Entrepreneur-2026' fair to boost youth employment and initiatives
item.description: Tashkent held the 'Future Entrepreneur-2026' career, employment, and entrepreneurship fair to connect youth with employers, banks, and educational institutions. Organized by several ministries and banks, the event provided information on job opportunities, training, and startup financing, including the 'Work with Pleasure' exhibition for job seekers.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey discuss cooperation in traditional crafts and cultural heritage
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan, led by the 'Hunarmand' association chairman, visited Turkey to discuss cooperation in developing traditional crafts and cultural heritage. Discussions included experience exchange and mutually beneficial projects, emphasizing the importance of preserving traditional craftsmanship for future generations.

item.title: Investigation into military tragedy in Mangystau reveals new details
item.description: An investigation is underway into the deaths of servicemen during military exercises in Kazakhstan's Mangystau region. Preliminary findings suggest negligence and violations of navigation rules. A government commission is determining all circumstances and responsible parties. Families of the deceased will receive financial aid.

item.title: Two criminal cases opened following Caspian Sea military tragedy in Aktau
item.description: Two criminal cases have been initiated following the deaths of servicemen during military exercises in the Caspian Sea near Aktau. Charges include "Negligent attitude to service" and "Violation of navigation rules." A government commission is investigating, and families of the deceased will receive state and private financial support.

item.title: Kazakhstan opens criminal case into military exercise deaths
item.description: Kazakhstan has opened a criminal case into the deaths of servicemen during military exercises in the Mangystau region. Charges include negligence and violating navigation rules. The government has pledged social and material support for the families of the deceased.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes phased pension system reform, increasing retirement age
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Economy and Finance has published a draft decree proposing phased pension system reforms, including a gradual increase in the retirement age. Starting January 1, 2028, the retirement age will rise by three months annually, reaching 63 for men and 58 for women by 2039. Protections against age-based dismissal are included.

item.title: Kazakhstan explains compensation eligibility from Victim's Fund
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office has outlined who can receive compensation from the Victim's Fund. This includes minors subjected to sexual violence, victims of trafficking and torture, and those who suffered severe harm or HIV infection due to crime.

item.title: Relatives mourn soldiers who died in Caspian Sea exercises
item.description: Relatives of soldiers who died during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea expressed grief, stating their sons were due home in a week. Parents are questioning the decision to conduct exercises during adverse weather conditions, despite storm warnings.

item.title: Kazakhstan Observes National Day of Mourning for Deceased Servicemen
item.description: Kazakhstan is observing a national day of mourning for 12 servicemen who died during naval exercises in the Mangystau region. The tragedy occurred due to severe weather conditions. Flags are lowered nationwide and at diplomatic missions abroad, and entertainment events have been canceled. Search operations for two missing servicemen are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Benin Agree to Visa Exemption for Diplomats
item.description: Holders of diplomatic and service passports from Kazakhstan and Benin will soon travel visa-free between the two countries. The agreement, signed on September 24 in New York, aims to simplify mutual travel and strengthen political and economic ties, according to Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Saida Mirziyoyeva Addresses UN General Assembly on Global Issues
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration of Uzbekistan, addressed the 81st UN General Assembly, outlining the country's stance on international security, trust-building, and Central Asian developments. She emphasized Uzbekistan's commitment to openness, good neighborliness, dialogue, and human dignity.

item.title: Taliban administration's security spending exceeds 45% of total expenditure, World Bank reports
item.description: Security spending by the Taliban administration accounted for over 45% of its total expenditure in the current fiscal year, according to a World Bank report. This spending reached 51.3 billion afghanis, approximately $787 million, surpassing combined outlays on education, health, agriculture, infrastructure, and private sector development.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Sentences Handed Down to Taftish.uz Staff and Former National Security Service Officers
item.description: Uzbekistan's Military Court has sentenced Taftish.uz editorial staff and former National Security Service (DXX) officers. The outlet's head received 10 years and 6 months, a journalist 4 years and 1 month, and two other staff members and former officers over 10 years. They were accused of defamation, insult, fraud, and extortion.

item.title: Halyk Fund provides 25 million tenge to families of fallen soldiers; Halyk Bank cancels their debts
item.description: The Halyk Fund has allocated 25 million tenge to support the families of military personnel who died during exercises on the Caspian Sea coast in the Mangystau region. Halyk Bank will fully write off the debts of the deceased servicemen. September 25 was declared a day of national mourning in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan views TRIPP route as extension of Middle Corridor, shortening European market access
item.description: Kazakhstan considers the TRIPP route a logical extension of the Middle Corridor, potentially shortening transport to European markets by about 1,000 kilometers. President Tokayev's representative stated this at the 7th Caspian Business Forum, highlighting TRIPP's strategic importance for connectivity with the South Caucasus, Türkiye, and Europe.

item.title: Kazakhstan Declares September 25 National Day of Mourning After Naval Exercise Tragedy
item.description: Kazakhstan declared September 25 a national day of mourning following a tragedy during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. Severe weather conditions caused 19 military personnel to be swept away by water. The death toll has now reached 12.

item.title: Families of deceased soldiers in Mangystau to receive 25 million tenge each from Shakhmyrat Mutalip
item.description: Businessman Shakhmyrat Mutalip announced that ERG and Integra Construction KZ companies will each donate 25 million tenge to the families of soldiers who died during exercises in the Mangystau region. This aid is in addition to state support. The tragedy occurred on September 24, with 12 soldiers confirmed dead and searches ongoing for two others.

item.title: Kandahar Bombing Injures Eight, Kills Seven at Mirwais Hospital
item.description: Seven people killed and eight injured in a Kandahar bombing were transferred to Mirwais Hospital. Sources report the injured were construction workers and some are in critical condition. Pakistani fighter jets reportedly bombed the Sarai Mullah Sahib area, a military headquarters.

item.title: Gadzhi Gadzhiyev pledges 100 million tenge to families of soldiers lost at sea
item.description: Prominent entrepreneur Gadzhi Gadzhiyev will provide 100 million tenge to the families of soldiers who died during Caspian Sea exercises. The incident on September 24 involved 17 servicemen being swept out to sea due to severe weather. Twelve died, three were rescued, and two remain missing. A government commission is investigating.

item.title: Members of the People's Council of Kazakhstan to provide financial aid to families of deceased soldiers
item.description: Seventeen members of the People's Council of Kazakhstan, primarily business representatives, have pledged a total of 815 million tenge to support the families of soldiers who died during Caspian Sea exercises. Individual contributions range from 1 million to 100 million tenge. The aid will be directly transferred to the families.

item.title: Kazakhstan Council Members Pledge 100 Million Tenge Aid to Families of Fallen Soldiers
item.description: Members of the People's Council of Kazakhstan announced financial assistance for the families of soldiers who died during Caspian Sea exercises. Businessman Shahmurat Mutalip stated that Integra Construction KZ will provide 25 million tenge to each family, in addition to state support. Another council member, Gadzhi Gadzhiev, confirmed the decision to allocate 100 million tenge in total.

item.title: Head of Supreme Shia Council Freed from Taliban Justice Minister's Custody
item.description: Mohammad Ali Akhlaqi, head of the Supreme Shia Council, was released from the personal prison of the Taliban's Justice Minister. He and another council member were reportedly tortured and forced to pledge not to engage in political activities. Their homes were vacated.

item.title: US and Iran Explore Phased Deal to End War, Reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: US and Iranian negotiators are considering a phased agreement to end the war. Under the proposal, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and the US would lift its economic blockade. Resuming free passage through the strait is a key US demand.

item.title: Vice Premier Bozymbayev Addresses Mangystau Situation, Promises Accountability
item.description: Vice Prime Minister Kanat Bozymbayev made a statement regarding the tragic events in Mangystau, where twelve servicemen died and three were rescued. A government commission has been formed to investigate. Bozymbayev assured that all responsible officials will be held strictly accountable and that families of the deceased will receive substantial material assistance.

item.title: Government Commission Head Vows Punishment for All Responsible in Tragedy
item.description: The head of the government commission, Kanat Bozumbayev, promised a thorough and objective investigation into a recent tragedy. He assured that all officials whose actions or inaction contributed to the disaster would face legal consequences. Families of deceased servicemen will receive substantial financial aid and support.

item.title: Names of 12 deceased soldiers released after Caspian Sea incident
item.description: Twelve military personnel drowned in the Caspian Sea during a training exercise in the Mangystau region. Three were rescued, and search efforts continue for two missing soldiers. The Ministry of Defense has published the names of the deceased servicemen.

item.title: Kazakhstan People's Council members pledge financial aid to families of deceased soldiers
item.description: Members of the Kazakhstan People's Council and entrepreneurs have pledged financial assistance to the families of soldiers who died during Caspian Sea exercises. One member will donate 25 million tenge per family, while another pledged 100 million tenge in total.

item.title: Taliban claim attack on Pakistani border post in Kandahar
item.description: The Taliban's Al-Badr 205 Corps claims to have attacked a Pakistani border post in the Spinboldak district of Kandahar. A spokesperson stated that a Pakistani military post was destroyed and inflicted heavy casualties after Pakistani forces allegedly fired mortar shells into the area.

item.title: Kazakh Deputy PM Promises Strict Punishment for Those Responsible for Military Deaths
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev stated that all officials whose actions or inaction led to the deaths of 12 servicemen in Mangystau will face severe legal consequences. The state will provide substantial financial and other support to the families of the deceased. Search efforts continue for two missing servicemen.

item.title: Rising Suicide Figures in Afghanistan Raise Serious Concerns
item.description: Multiple reports of suicide incidents from different Afghan provinces in a single day highlight a worrying trend. The true scale of the phenomenon remains unknown due to difficulties in recording and reporting, but scattered reports suggest the issue requires serious attention.
